content:
maya: heads up — during the int4 bring-up for `hera-70b` we're seeing output bias start around token 48k. small divergence that grows with longer contexts :thinking_face:

sahil: can you paste the repro? is this during prefill or after continuous generation?

maya: repro is prefill -> continue. short summary: exact same prompt, fp16 vs int4 diverge after ~48k, int4 tends to hallucinate repeated filler tokens. looks like KV saturation or RoPE wrap interaction.

ophelia: interesting. did you try scaling RoPE (freq_scale) or clamping rotary phase like we did for other models?

maya: tried freq_scale=1.02 and 0.98 quickly — small impact but divergence point moves by only ~500 tokens.

lucas: can you run the quick smoke with KV window diagnostic enabled? add `KV_DUMP=on` env and run the same seed. will get index fingerprints.

maya: running now locally. command: ```
KV_DUMP=on ./run_infer --model=hera-70b-int4 --seed=42 --max-tokens=52000 --prefill-file=longtest_prompt.txt
```

ci-bot: test-run 1745009999-1 started on runner-12 (hera-70b-int4). logs: https://ci.internal/1745009999-1 :robot_face:

raman: fiducial check — did you check per-layer kv norms? quant noise tends to amplify in later layers if kv scaling not adjusted.

maya: attached small excerpt of KV index diff (from KV_DUMP): ```
layer42: idx=12048 -> 12048  (match)
layer43: idx=12400 -> 12401  (off-by-1)
layer44: idx=12800 -> 12803  (drift)
... drift increases after layer 48
```

sahil: off-by-1 at multiple layers smells like tiling/stride mismatch after int4 packing. maybe our memcpy alignment for packed KV is miscomputed for certain sequence lengths. check prefill stride and pad bytes.

ophelia: also check rotary embedding interpolation path — for extremely long contexts we sometimes fall back to a slower path that truncates precision. if int4 fallback interacts with that path it could create phase mismatch.

maya: reproduce log snippet (truncated): ```
[2026-03-10T14:22:10Z] prefill tokens=48000 consumed=48000
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] kv_write: shard0 offset=9830400 bytes=245760
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] kv_write: shard0 offset=10086400 bytes=245760
[2026-03-10T14:22:17Z] attention: rotary_wrap_detected layer=47 pos=48012
[2026-03-10T14:22:20Z] gen: output repeating token_id=502 seqlen=48040
```

lucas: thanks. next steps: 1) bisect prefill stride/pad change, 2) run same test on int8 and fp16 to confirm behavior, 3) check memcpy pad for kernel version v2.1.

raman: for quant experiments, also try running with `KV_CACHE_FRACTION=0.75` (reduced effective KV window) to see if reducing cache size prevents overflow-induced wrap. we've had similar cases where smaller effective window avoids the phase rollover.

maya: quick result: int8 run didn't diverge up to 56k. fp16 stable. with KV_CACHE_FRACTION=0.75 int4 pushed divergence to ~51k. so seems related to effective KV capacity + quant noise.

sahil: that's a helpful signal. hypothesis: packed-int4 layout causes occasional stride rounding that only shows up when the cache hits certain boundaries, causing small index shifts which with RoPE accumulate into phase misalignment and token drift.

ophelia: could be reproducible with a synthetic that fills the KV with deterministic pattern then reads back. want me to craft that microtest?

maya: yes please — would speed root cause. also we should file a canary for dedicated infra so customers on long-context workloads are alerted.

ci-bot: test-run 1745009999-1 completed: status=failed, reproduction found (divergence at token 48040). artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/1745009999-1/kv_dump.tar.gz

lucas: assigning a quick ticket to eng-runtime to run the memcpy/pack audit. I'll include the log excerpts and KV dump.

raman: note for release playbook — if we can't get a stable int4 roll for 70b with >50k contexts, add a gating rule: autopromote int8 only for workflows with max_context > 50k.

maya: agreeing. will add to onboarding checklist: "long-context stress with KV_DUMP and KV_CACHE_FRACTION sweep". tagging follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
